official_sources.establishes: least-privilege GITHUB_TOKEN permissions, safe secret handling, SHA pinning for third-party actions, OIDC preference for cloud auth, and runner hardening considerations
concurrency cancellation/queuing can prevent duplicate stale jobs and reduce conflicts/cost
Rust CI should build/test with cargo and may cache Cargo dependencies when Cargo.lock is present
cache dependencies/build outputs for reuse and reserve artifacts for post-run outputs/logs
prompt injection can come from third-party/untrusted content; layered defenses, monitoring, red-teaming, least-access, and confirmations for consequential actions reduce risk
AI RMF and generative AI profile support risk management, trustworthiness, evaluation, and governance for AI systems
OWASP LLM risks include prompt injection, insecure output handling, sensitive information disclosure, excessive agency, and model denial of service
Step Functions Retry/Catch model, exponential backoff controls, timeout retry/catch semantics, and heartbeat timeout error availability for Retry/Catch.
Task states define Retry, Catch, TimeoutSeconds, HeartbeatSeconds, and recommended timeout/heartbeat settings for long-running activities.
Google Workflows retry policies define retry predicates, maximum retries, and backoff with initial delay, max delay, and multiplier; idempotent and non-idempotent policies are distinct.
Default retry policy is intended for idempotent targets and retries selected transient HTTP/connection/timeout errors with bounded retries/backoff.
Temporal retry policies are declarative; activities retry by default with exponential backoff, workflows generally do not retry by default, and non-retryable errors should surface permanent failures.
Durable orchestration uses event sourcing, deterministic replay, durable timers for timeout handling, external events, and activity/sub-orchestrator retry policies.
Apache TinkerPop Gremlin models graph traversal with repeat()/times() loops, emit/until traversal control, and path output; supports bounded iterative traversal semantics for this preview BFS slice.
PostgreSQL recursive query guidance emphasizes iterative evaluation, explicit termination, cycle detection, and practical limits for loop-prone recursive graph queries.
SPARQL 1.1 property paths define graph connectivity over named directed edges, path length operators, duplicate suppression for connectivity, and cycle-safe finite matching semantics.
Neo4j Cypher variable-length/quantified path guidance recommends finite upper bounds, specific relationship/node predicates, and pruning to avoid path explosion.

AWS Builders Library recommends caller-provided request identifiers, semantically equivalent replay responses, auditable idempotency tokens, and atomic coupling of token recording with side effects for safe retries.
Stripe compares repeated idempotency-key request parameters with the original request and errors when they differ, preventing accidental key misuse.
OpenTelemetry log guidance supports structured events and correlation with trace/span context and resource context across logs, traces, and metrics.

CloudTrail audit-event records capture action timing, request/response metadata, read/write classification, resources, account context, and shared event identifiers for cross-account action correlation.
